title: The Past Participle as an Adjective: elkészített étel

sections.title: Turning a verb into a describing word
sections.content: Every verb you already conjugate in the past tense (the -t/-tt form: készített, írt, épített) can also work as an adjective, placed directly before a noun, exactly where any other adjective goes. elkészített étel literally means "prepared food" — a meal described by what happened to it. The participle itself never changes shape for case or number; only the noun after it inflects normally.

sections.title: The participle sits still, the noun inflects

items.spanish: Szeretem az anyám által elkészített ételeket.
items.english: I love the meals prepared by my mother.
I found the key that had long been lost.
This is a carefully written letter.

sections.content: által ("by") names who did the action, the same job English "...-ed by" does: az anyám által elkészített étel, "the meal prepared by my mother". Drop által and the sentence still works, it just stops saying who — elkészített étel, simply "prepared food".
